DMart Shares Hit 52-Week Low Amid Analyst Target Divergence

Avenue Supermarts, the company behind DMart, saw its shares fall to a 52-week low of ₹3,366 on Tuesday, opening at ₹3,405 and dropping 4.4% from its previous close. Over a six-month period, the stock has declined 23%, a steeper fall than the 7% loss experienced by the Sensex. Analysts from Bernstein, JPMorgan, HSBC, and Goldman Sachs have set divergent price targets for the stock, with some suggesting a potential fall to ₹3,214 while others project a rise to ₹5,723.
